note: Calcimimetics lower PTH in dialysis patients exactly as the 5/6-nephrectomy rat said, but the rat's vascular-calcification benefit never became a survival or cardiovascular benefit (EVOLVE).
label: SHPT (calcimimetics)

engagement.note: NPS R-568, cinacalcet's precursor, halved parathyroid-cell proliferation in 5/6-nephrectomised rats; cinacalcet's own rat PTH suppression came in Nemeth 2004.
engagement.short: Calcimimetic engages parathyroid in uraemic rats
engagement.quote: Low and high doses of NPS R-568 reduced the number of BrdU-positive PT cells by 20 and 50%, respectively.

engagement.note: Rats: dose-dependent PTH and ionised-calcium fall (Nemeth 2004). Patients: PTH -43% on cinacalcet vs +9% on placebo over 26 weeks.
engagement.quote: Overall, mean parathyroid hormone values decreased 43 percent in those receiving cinacalcet but increased 9 percent in the placebo group (P<0.001).
engagement.reason: PTH fell in patients as in rats
engagement.judgement: My juxtaposition of Nemeth 2004 (rat, doi:10.1124/jpet.103.057273) with Block 2004 (patients); no source states both. The pivotal trials (NCT00037635, NCT00527267; start 2001-2002) have no results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov. Etelcalcetide repeated the match: 5/6-nephrectomy rats (Walter 2013, doi:10.1124/jpet.113.204834) then 74-75% of patients with >30% PTH reduction (Block 2017, doi:10.1001/jama.2016.19456; NCT01785849/NCT01788046 results posted 2017-03-27). No status change, so no extra entry.

dose.note: Cinacalcet lowered PTH and ionised calcium dose-dependently at 1-36 mg/kg oral with linear PK in rats; no patient exposure target was stated.
dose.quote: In vivo studies in rats demonstrated cinacalcet HCl is orally bioavailable and displays approximately linear pharmacokinetics over the dose range of 1 to 36 mg/kg.

dose.note: EMA: the on-target hypocalcaemia that limits animal dosing appears at exposures close to clinical exposure, so the pharmacologically active exposure carried over to patients.
dose.short: Animal active exposure matches clinical exposure
dose.quote: However, the occurrence of non-tolerable hypocalcaemia already at exposure levels close to the clinical exposure severely limits the possibility to establish appropriate safety margins.
dose.judgement: Judgement call. The EMA sentence is a safety-margin statement, not an efficacy exposure target, but the exposure it refers to is the on-target CaSR effect (calcium lowering), so I read it as the model's active exposure holding in patients. The same review says animals get substantially lower AUC/Cmax per mg/kg than humans, so mg/kg doses do not translate but exposure does; the only number is a dog Cmax 1.6-fold above human Cmax at the maximum dose, which is the basis for within_2x. EMA reviews are not in the brief's rule-1 whitelist (FDA/DOI/registry); downgrade to untested if the whitelist is strict. Document carries 'EMEA 2004' page footers; EC approval 2004-10-22.

efficacy.note: NPS R-568 suppressed parathyroid-cell proliferation in 5/6-nephrectomised rats; cinacalcet later shrank parathyroids and suppressed aortic calcification in the same model (Kawata 2008).
efficacy.quote: These results indicate that NPS R-568 suppresses PT cell proliferation in rats with renal insufficiency, and lend support to the linkage between the CaR and PT hyperplasia in CRI.

efficacy.note: The disease as defined responded: 43% reached iPTH of 250 pg/mL or less vs 5% on placebo, CaxP -15%, as the uraemic rat predicted.
efficacy.quote: Forty-three percent of the cinacalcet group reached the primary end point, as compared with 5 percent of the placebo group (P<0.001).
efficacy.judgement: SHPT is defined by PTH, so the biomarker response counts as the disease responding; the hard-endpoint question is carried by the 2012 entry.

efficacy.note: Rats on cinacalcet had less aortic calcification (Kawata 2008); in patients EVOLVE's death/CV composite was HR 0.93 (0.85-1.02) and ADVANCE missed its CAC endpoint.
efficacy.short: No death/CV benefit despite PTH control
efficacy.quote: In an unadjusted intention-to-treat analysis, cinacalcet did not significantly reduce the risk of death or major cardiovascular events in patients with moderate-to-severe secondary hyperparathyroidism who were undergoing dialysis.
efficacy.reason: Rat calcification gain, no patient outcome
efficacy.judgement: Two calls. (1) contra rather than same: the biomarker matched, but the rat's hard-endpoint prediction, less vascular calcification (Kawata 2008, doi:10.1038/ki.2008.407, cinacalcet in 5/6-nephrectomy rats; Walter 2013 for etelcalcetide), did not become patient benefit: ADVANCE (Raggi 2011, doi:10.1093/ndt/gfq725, NCT00379899, results posted 2010-10-27) missed its primary Agatston CAC endpoint (24% vs 31%, P=0.073) and EVOLVE (NCT00345839, results posted 2014-01-22) missed death/CV events. (2) 2012 rather than 2011: ADVANCE's authors framed their result as 'may attenuate' calcification (volume and valve scores favoured cinacalcet), so it does not establish a contradiction on its own; EVOLVE does. A stricter reader could move the contra to 2011. No primary source puts rat and patient results side by side; I juxtaposed them, and I read EVOLVE at abstract level (NEJM full text not accessed). The rat never had a mortality endpoint, so the miss is on the inference chain PTH -> calcification -> events, not on a rat-measured outcome. EVOLVE's parathyroidectomy reduction (secondary) does match the rat hyperplasia data.

safety.note: Rats dosed with cinacalcet lost ionised calcium dose-dependently, naming hypocalcaemia as the on-target liability; dog and monkey toxicology added emesis (EMA 2004).
safety.quote: Furthermore, this compound suppressed serum PTH and blood-ionized Ca(2+) levels and increased serum calcitonin levels in a dose-dependent manner.

safety.note: Hypocalcaemia held: calcium <8.4 mg/dL in 66% vs 25%, <7.5 in 5% vs <1%; nausea 31%/vomiting 27% matched animal emesis.
safety.quote: In the 26-week studies of patients with CKD on dialysis, 66% of patients receiving Sensipar™ compared with 25% of patients receiving placebo developed at least one serum calcium value < 8.4 mg/dL.
safety.judgement: The label carries the 66%/25% calcium and the nausea 31% vs 19% / vomiting 27% vs 15% rates; the 5% vs <1% figure for calcium <7.5 mg/dL and the animal findings ('hypocalcaemia ... was the dose-limiting toxicity in most species'; 'frequent emesis' in dogs, 'sporadic emesis' in monkeys) are in the EMA 2004 scientific discussion. The rat alone cannot vomit, so the GI prediction rests on dog/monkey toxicology, hence the three-species model name. Rule 5: the comparison existed in 2004 (label approved 2004-03-08), so the model entry and the match share a year. EVOLVE 2012 ('Hypocalcemia and gastrointestinal adverse events were significantly more frequent in patients receiving cinacalcet') and etelcalcetide 2017 ('decreased blood calcium' the most common adverse effect, 68.9% vs 59.8% vs cinacalcet, doi:10.1001/jama.2016.19468) repeated the match; no status change.
